title: Natural or made by people? Sorting materials

figure.name: x-sort
figure.question: Did nature make it, or did people?

explain.say: Look at your T-shirt. If it is cotton, it grew in a field, on a fluffy plant! Some materials come straight from nature, and some are made by people, often from natural things. Let's sort them out.

draw.text: Natural or made by people? Sorting materials

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Did nature make it, or did people?

explain.say: See the Natural group lighting up? Natural materials come from plants, animals or the ground. Wood from trees, wool from sheep, cotton from plants, stone from the earth, and silk spun by silkworms in China. Which natural material are you wearing?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Did nature make it, or did people?

explain.say: Now Made by people glows. Plastic, glass, paper, nylon and steel do not grow anywhere. People make them in factories by changing natural things. Paper is made from wood, and plastic is mostly made from oil. Can you spot something plastic near you?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Did nature make it, or did people?

explain.say: Let's watch glass being made. See the hot furnace light up? Sand is heated hotter than 1400 degrees, until it melts into a glowing, runny liquid. That is far hotter than any kitchen oven! Can you guess what happens next?

explain.say: Glass makers blow it, press it or pour it flat, and as it cools it becomes hard, see-through glass. Wonderful sorting! Wow fact: one silkworm cocoon is made from a single silk thread that can be nearly a kilometre long.

faq.a: A natural material is found in nature or grows there, like wood, cotton, wool, silk, stone, sand and clay. We may cut or clean it, but we do not change what it is.
Paper is made by people. Wood is mashed into a pulp with water, pressed flat and dried, which changes it into a new material.
Sand, mixed with soda and limestone, is heated in a furnace to over 1400 degrees Celsius until it melts. The runny glass is shaped and then cooled until it is hard and clear.
Most plastic is made from oil or natural gas, changed in factories into long chain-like molecules. Some newer plastics are made from plants like maize or sugar cane.
Silk comes from the cocoons of silkworms, which are caterpillars of a moth. People in China discovered how to unwind the thread thousands of years ago.

facts: Glass is made by melting sand (silica) with soda ash and limestone at around 1400 to 1600 °C.
A single silkworm cocoon can be made of one continuous thread several hundred metres to nearly a kilometre long.

quiz.say: Which of these materials is natural?
quiz.why: Wool grows on sheep, so it is natural.

wrong.0: Plastic is made by people, mostly from oil.
wrong.2: Nylon is a material made by people in factories.

quiz.why: Glass is made by melting sand at very high temperatures.

wrong.1: Wood is used to make paper, not glass.
wrong.2: Wool is used for clothes, not glass.
